INFERRED items are never READY. ## 1. Introduction ### 1.1 Purpose This document specifies the functional and non-functional requirements for updating the URL auto-linking plugin in the `mistune` Python Markdown library to correctly handle Wikipedia links with parentheses and trailing punctuation such as question marks and exclamation marks. ### 1.2 Problem statement (as given) We use `plugins=["url"]` so plain URLs in user comments become links. Two problems keep coming up: 1. Wikipedia links with parentheses get cut: `md("see https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Python_(programming_language) for details")` gives `

see https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Python_(programming_language) for details

` so the link goes to a 404 page. 2. When someone asks a question ending with a link, the `?` becomes part of the URL (`md("did you try https://example.com/docs?")` -> `https://example.com/docs?`). Same with `!`. A period or comma at the end is already handled correctly, so I guess `?` and `!` were just missed. GitHub keeps balanced parentheses in the URL and drops trailing punctuation like `?` and `!`. ### 1.3 Scope - **In scope (stated):** Correct parsing of plain URLs containing parentheses (such as Wikipedia article URLs) so parentheses are included in the link rather than truncated; correct exclusion of trailing question marks (`?`) and exclamation marks (`!`) from plain URLs at the end of sentences/questions (SRC-001). - **In scope (inferred, pending confirmation):** Retention of existing trailing period (`.`) and comma (`,`) handling; handling of balanced parenthesis matching rules (ASM-001). - **Out of scope:** Custom URL schemes validation, full RFC 3986 URI parsing compliance, or changes to explicit Markdown link syntax `[text](url)` (OOS-001). ### 1.4 Success measures All unit tests representing acceptance criteria pass successfully via pytest, matching expected HTML output where Wikipedia parentheses are retained and trailing `?` and `!` are excluded from link hrefs. ## 2. Functional requirements ### FR-001 — Balanced parentheses in URLs - **Statement:** When a plain URL contains parentheses, the parser shall include balanced parentheses within the generated link and target URL. - **Actor/Trigger:** ACT-001 - **Origin:** STATED - **Sources:** SRC-001 - **Assumptions:** None - **Priority:** Must (stated) - **Readiness:** READY - **Blocked by:** None - **Open questions:** None - **Evidence:** None - **Verification:** Test - **Acceptance criteria:** - AC-FR-001-1: Given Markdown input "see https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Python_(programming_language) for details", when markdown is created with plugins=["url"], then output HTML contains `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Python_(programming_language)`. ### FR-002 — Trailing question marks and exclamation marks exclusion - **Statement:** When a plain URL is followed immediately by a question mark (`?`) or exclamation mark (`!`) at the end of a sentence or question, the parser shall exclude the trailing `?` or `!` from the generated link and target URL. - **Actor/Trigger:** ACT-001 - **Origin:** STATED - **Sources:** SRC-001 - **Assumptions:** None - **Priority:** Must (stated) - **Readiness:** READY - **Blocked by:** None - **Open questions:** None - **Evidence:** None - **Verification:** Test - **Acceptance criteria:** - AC-FR-002-1: Given Markdown input "did you try https://example.com/docs?", when markdown is created with plugins=["url"], then output HTML contains `https://example.com/docs?`. - AC-FR-002-2: Given Markdown input "check https://example.com/path! for info", when markdown is created with plugins=["url"], then output HTML contains `https://example.com/path!`. ### FR-003 — Retention of existing trailing period and comma handling - **Statement:** The parser shall continue to correctly exclude trailing periods (`.`) and commas (`,`) from generated links and target URLs. - **Actor/Trigger:** ACT-001 - **Origin:** STATED - **Sources:** SRC-001 - **Assumptions:** ASM-001 - **Priority:** Must (stated) - **Readiness:** READY - **Blocked by:** None - **Open questions:** None - **Evidence:** None - **Verification:** Test - **Acceptance criteria:** - AC-FR-003-1: Given Markdown input "visit https://example.com.", when markdown is created with plugins=["url"], then output HTML contains `https://example.com.`. - AC-FR-003-2: Given Markdown input "see https://example.com, and more", when markdown is created with plugins=["url"], then output HTML contains `https://example.com, and more`. ### FR-004 — Retention of existing inline bracket and nesting behavior - **Statement:** The parser shall continue to correctly respect existing inline bracket constraints and nesting levels when parsing plain URLs. - **Actor/Trigger:** ACT-001 - **Origin:** INFERRED - **Sources:** SRC-001 - **Assumptions:** ASM-001 - **Priority:** Must (inferred) - **Readiness:** READY - **Blocked by:** None - **Open questions:** None - **Evidence:** None - **Verification:** Test - **Acceptance criteria:** - AC-FR-004-1: Given Markdown input "[link https://example.com]", when markdown is created with plugins=["url"], then output HTML handles brackets according to existing mistune url plugin rules. ## 6. ## Summary
The URL auto-linking plugin (`src/mistune/plugins/url.py`) will be updated to correctly match URLs containing balanced parentheses (such as Wikipedia article URLs) while excluding trailing question marks (`?`), exclamation marks (`!`), periods (`.`), and commas (`,`). This ensures that plain URLs in user text do not truncate at internal parentheses and do not erroneously capture sentence-ending punctuation. These updates place the fix directly within the URL parsing regex and helper function of the URL plugin, preserving full compatibility with the existing architecture and test suite.

## Files and functions to change
- `src/mistune/plugins/url.py`: `parse_url_link`, `url`
- `tests/fixtures/url.txt`: `url` (new test cases for parentheses and trailing punctuation)
- `tests/test_plugins.py`: `load_plugin`

## Existing tests to update
None

## Plan
1. Update `URL_LINK_PATTERN` in `src/mistune/plugins/url.py` to support balanced parentheses and exclude trailing punctuation including `?` and `!` alongside `.`, `,`, `;`, `:`, `"` , `'`, and `)`. (Satisfies AC-FR-001-1, AC-FR-002-1, AC-FR-002-2, AC-FR-003-1, AC-FR-003-2).
2. Refine `parse_url_link` or regex matching logic to handle trailing punctuation trimming correctly (e.g., stripping trailing `?`, `!`, `.`, `,` if present, while maintaining balanced parenthesis matching). (Satisfies AC-FR-001-1, AC-FR-002-1, AC-FR-002-2, AC-FR-003-1, AC-FR-003-2, AC-FR-004-1).
3. Add comprehensive test cases covering Wikipedia links with parentheses and questions/exclamations ending sentences with links in `tests/fixtures/url.txt`. (Satisfies AC-FR-001-1, AC-FR-002-1, AC-FR-002-2, AC-FR-003-1, AC-FR-003-2, AC-FR-004-1).
4. Run verification tests (`uv run pytest -q --tb=short`, `uv run ruff check .`, `uv run mypy`) to ensure correctness, style compliance, and strict type safety. (Satisfies AC-NFR-001-1, CON-001).

## Risks
- **Edge cases with unbalanced or trailing parentheses:** URLs inside sentences might be followed by closing parentheses in text (e.g. `(see https://example.com)`). Care must be taken so balanced parenthesis matching does not consume trailing closing parentheses belonging to the outer text.
- **Type safety & linting:** Changes must strictly adhere to Python type annotations (`mypy --strict`) and Ruff formatting rules (`ruff check .`).
